facts.text: Middle Village earned its name because it sat midway between Williamsburg and Jamaica on the old stagecoach route.
Juniper Valley Park, opened in 1930, showcases the neighborhood’s evolution and is a prime example of local history.
The United Community Methodist Church, founded as the Methodist Episcopal Church of Newtown, is the first Methodist church in Middle Village.
The only extant synagogue, Congregation of Forest Hills West, was founded in 1935 after many earlier synagogues had closed.
The Juniper Park Civic Association, founded in 1938, became one of Queens’ most active groups, lobbying for playgrounds and infrastructure.
During the Revolutionary War, American soldiers hid in a swamp near what is now Middle Village, later marked by Juniper Round Swamp Road.
